sentences.text: Tupuxuara possessed a large crest extending from the back of its head to its snout.
The animal had a toothless beak.
The most distinguishing feature of this creature is a large bone crest protruding from the back of its head to its snout.
Its head, measuring nearly one meter, was enormous compared to the body and very lightweight due to holes in the skull.
Tupuxuara measured approximately 2.5 meters in length and 5.4 meters in wingspan.
Tupuxuara had an estimated wingspan of 4.7 meters and a body mass of 25 kilograms.
The largest skulls have a length of 130 centimeters, indicating a wingspan of 5.5 meters.
Its main distinguishing feature was a large head crest that was more rounded in females and absent in individuals that had not reached sexual maturity.
The genus Tupuxuara was described by paleontologists Kellner and Campos in 1988.
The holotype specimen of Tupuxuara longicristatus (MN 6591-V) was found in the Santana Formation, now called the Romualdo Formation, in Brazil.
A second species, Tupuxuara leonardii, was named in 1994 by Kellner and Campos.
Tupuxuara longicristatus was discovered in the Santana Formation in 1988 by Alexander Kellner and Diógenes Campos.
There are 5 recorded fossil occurrences of Tupuxuara.
Researchers suggest the crest size likely indicates sexual maturity, as it appears more prominent in mature individuals.
Based on its lineage, Tupuxuara was likely a terrestrial omnivore or carnivore, contrary to earlier suggestions of a fish or fruit diet.
It has been suggested that Tupuxuara had a piscivorous diet preying on the coasts of modern-day South America, while some hypotheses include the possibility that it was a fruit eater.
Tupuxuara was initially assigned to the family Tapejaridae by Kellner, closely related to the pterosaur Tapejara.
In 2007, Kellner and Campos placed Tupuxuara in the subfamily Thalassodrominae alongside Thalassodromeus.
Kellner assigned Tupuxuara to the family Tapejaridae within Azhdarchoidea.
The genus authority for Tupuxuara is Kellner & Campos, 1988.
Tupuxuara is a member of the Azhdarchoidea group.
The parent group of Tupuxuara is Thalassodromidae.
Recent studies suggest Tupuxuara deliradamus should be removed from the genus Tupuxuara and placed in the subfamily Tapejarinae.
Tupuxuara lived during the Albian age of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago.
Tupuxuara was a pterodactyloid pterosaur of the superfamily Azhdarchoidea that lived in the Early Cretaceous (Valanginian and Hauterivian stages) in what is now Brazil.
Tupuxuara lived during the Aptian stage, from 119.57 to 113.2 million years ago.
Some studies argue Tupuxuara belongs in the family Thalassodromidae rather than Tapejaridae, based on a closer relationship with Azhdarchidae and Dsungaripteridae.
Some analyses suggest Tupuxuara is more closely related to the Azhdarchidae family, which includes the giant Texas Quetzalcoatlus, than to Tapejara and its relatives.
It is debated whether Tupuxuara deliradamus is a valid species, as it has been classified as a nomen dubium by Kellner in 2013 and by Cerqueira et al. in 2023.
